submission.justification: Module-D2 has the highest light yield (38 PE/MeV at 20% coverage) but fails the hard thermal-cycling limit: 30% of modules fail after 20 cycles versus the 5% maximum, and failed modules cannot be replaced. That rules it out. Module-D1 passes thermally (0.5%) but gives only 18 PE/MeV at 20%. Module-D3 passes (2% failed) and gives 27 PE/MeV at 20%, the best light yield among the compliant designs. Light yield rises roughly as coverage^0.8, so I chose the maximum allowed coverage of 30%, which the meeting notes say the feedthroughs support. The expected yield at 30% is about 27 x (30/20)^0.8 = ~37 PE/MeV. This is an extrapolation from the 2025 simulation, not a direct simulation at 30%, so it should be checked before final design freeze.

requirements.requirement: Module must be one of the three candidate designs
requirements.evidence: Module-D3 (WLS bar with SiPM readout) is listed in candidate_specs.md.

requirements.requirement: At most 5% of modules fail after 20 thermal cycles (hard requirement)
requirements.evidence: query_thermal_cycling returned 2.0% failed for Module-D3 (thermal_cycling_tests.md: 2% of a 40-module batch).
Recommended coverage is 30%, the upper bound; feedthroughs support up to 30% per the 2026-01-20 meeting notes.
Module-D3 gives 27 PE/MeV at 20% coverage, the highest of the compliant designs (D1: 18). Estimated ~37 PE/MeV at 30% by coverage^0.8 scaling; the 30% value is extrapolated, not simulated.
